slides.headline: EVERY EXIT OUT OF SOUTH VIETNAM WAS ALREADY GONE
slides.body:
April 29, 1975. The last morning of the war.

Roads cut. Airfields overrun. Major Buang-Ly had a two-seat observation plane and an idea
slides.image_prompt: Abandoned South Vietnamese military aircraft on a damaged tarmac, smoke billowing from bombed hangars, silhouetted civilian figures rushing toward a chain-link fence, thick amber haze under a vivid red late-afternoon sky; documentary news photo, 35mm, film grain; accent: smoldering amber against smoky khaki.

slides.headline: HE CIRCLED THE CARRIER AND DROPPED A NOTE FROM THE COCKPIT
slides.body: No radio contact with the USS Midway. No clearance. No plan except the one in his hands. He flew over the deck and dropped a handwritten note from the cockpit, asking permission to land.
slides.image_prompt: A folded white paper note tumbling through open blue sky, a vast carrier flight deck visible far below with tiny figures, a small propeller plane silhouette circling above; documentary news photo, 35mm, film grain; accent: cream white paper against deep steel-blue ocean.

slides.headline: THE CAPTAIN ORDERED THE CREW TO PUSH HELICOPTERS INTO THE OCEAN
slides.body: Captain Lawrence Chambers gave the order. Helicopters worth millions got shoved off the flight deck, one by one. Imagine watching your most valuable equipment go overboard for a stranger.

slides.headline: NO TAILHOOK. HE LANDED ANYWAY.
slides.body: Every carrier landing in history requires one. He had none

slides.headline: SEVEN PEOPLE ESCAPED VIETNAM IN A PLANE BUILT FOR TWO
slides.body: The Cessna O-1 Bird Dog held one pilot and one observer. Two seats. Buang-Ly flew his wife and five children out of Con Son Island. The plane is still in Pensacola, Florida.

caption:
Swipe through the true story of Major Buang-Ly, the South Vietnamese pilot who landed on the USS Midway during the fall of Saigon by dropping a handwritten note from his cockpit.

The fall of Saigon, April 29 1975, Major Buang-Ly, his wife and five children, Con Son Island, a two-seat Cessna O-1 Bird Dog, every exit already closed, the USS Midway spotted from the air, a handwritten note dropped from the cockpit, Captain Lawrence Chambers reading it on the deck, the order to clear the flight deck, helicopters pushed overboard into the sea, a plane with no tailhook completing a carrier landing, a family of seven escaping to freedom, the Cessna preserved today at the National Naval Aviation Museum in Pensacola, Florida.

There are moments where someone refuses to accept it's over and finds a way through anyway. Buang-Ly made that landing with no backup plan and no second chance. Running a business? DM us "AI" and we'll show you what this could do for yours.
